slo_alignment_summary: Customer wants a clear definition for p50/p95/p99 across streaming and non-streaming flows. Proposal: measure both client-side end-to-end and server-side server-processing-only. Streaming SLOs measured on 'time-to-first-token' (TTFT) and 'time-to-last-token' (TTLT) for full-response p95/p99. Non-streaming measured as total request latency (server receive -> last byte sent). Agree to expose both metrics in Console and include sample-based percentiles plus synthetic probes in NA region.
measurement_details:
- Client-side: instrument SDK to report start->first-byte and start->complete; aggregate via telemetry.
- Server-side: use request timing from ingress -> egress; correlate with KV cache hits to explain variance.
- Stream: define TTFT p95 <= 200ms target, TTLT p95 depends on token count; will normalize to per-100-token TTLT baseline.
- Non-stream: target p95 <= 800ms, p99 <= 1.5s (initial).
throughput_requirements: Sustained throughput target: 12k tokens/sec across reserved pool during market hours (~08:30-16:00 ET). Burst capacity: 2x sustained for 10-minute spikes. Expect continuous batching to be enabled, but customer wants deterministic worst-case per-session latency guarantees.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial sizing: 6 x A100-ish nodes equivalent (customer workload estimate), configured as 4 reserved + 2 burst on Dedicated. Include plan to run 72h replay to validate before contract. Autoscale policy: strict upper cap to protect SLA; pre-warm KV cache before market open.
sla_negotiation_notes:
- Customer requires SLA language around p95 latency breaches during peak windows with credits tied to sustained daily breach.
- They want explicit fallbacks: automatic model fallback to a smaller variant with documented quality regression thresholds.
- Legal asking for 'time-to-recover' metric and runbook; Redwood to provide incident templates.
- Pricing negotiable if Redwood fronts part of cost for burst capacity during first 6 months.
